learning_goal: Place both kidneys on the posterior abdominal wall against T12 to L3, say why the right sits lower than the left, name the coverings from the renal capsule out to the pararenal fat, order the structures in the hilum from front to back and the layers from cortex to pelvis, trace blood in by the renal artery and out by the renal vein, and use that anatomy to explain the loin approach, the loin-to-groin pain of a stone and why the left renal vein is the vulnerable one.

terms: front to back in the hilum
one point two litres per minute

structures.name: right kidney
structures.label: Right kidney
structures.narration: A bean-shaped organ about eleven centimetres long, six wide and three thick, lying on the posterior abdominal wall behind the peritoneum. The right kidney sits about half a vertebral body lower than the left because the liver occupies the space above it — so it spans roughly the body of L1 to the body of L3, and its upper pole is crossed by the twelfth rib only. Its hilum faces medially and slightly forward, and the whole organ is tilted so that its anterior surface looks forward and laterally. In a thin patient the lower pole of the right kidney can be balloted bimanually on deep inspiration; the left almost never can.

structures.name: left kidney
structures.label: Left kidney
structures.narration: The left kidney is the higher of the two, spanning about T12 to L2, and it is crossed behind by both the eleventh and the twelfth ribs. Its hilum lies almost exactly on the transpyloric plane, at the level of the lower border of L1 — the single most useful level in the abdomen, because the pylorus, the neck of the pancreas, the fundus of the gallbladder and the origin of the superior mesenteric artery all sit on it. In front it is related to the stomach, the spleen, the tail of the pancreas, the splenic vessels, the left colic flexure and coils of jejunum.

structures.name: right renal artery
structures.label: Right renal artery — the longer one
structures.narration: Arises from the side of the aorta just below the origin of the superior mesenteric artery, at about the L1 to L2 disc. Because the aorta lies to the left of the midline, the right renal artery is the longer of the two and must pass behind the inferior vena cava to reach its kidney. It divides at the hilum into five segmental arteries, and those are functional end arteries — they do not anastomose, so occluding one infarcts its segment completely. Accessory renal arteries are common, usually reaching the lower pole, and they matter because an accessory artery divided at nephrectomy or transplantation kills the territory it supplied.

structures.name: left renal artery
structures.label: Left renal artery
structures.narration: Shorter than the right, because the aorta already lies on the left. Between them the two renal arteries carry about a fifth of the cardiac output — over a litre of blood a minute through organs that together weigh three hundred grams. That enormous flow is what makes the kidney so sensitive to a drop in perfusion, and it is why a narrowed renal artery drives renin, and with it secondary hypertension.

structures.name: right renal vein
structures.label: Right renal vein — the short one
structures.narration: Short and direct, because the inferior vena cava lies on the right. It receives no tributaries of consequence: the right gonadal vein and the right suprarenal vein drain straight into the cava instead. That asymmetry is the whole reason the right kidney is the harder one to take for transplantation — a short vein is difficult to anastomose.

structures.name: left renal vein
structures.label: Left renal vein — the long one, and the vulnerable one
structures.narration: Three times as long as the right, because it must cross the midline. It runs to the right in front of the aorta and behind the superior mesenteric artery to reach the cava, and that sandwich is the nutcracker: compression there raises pressure in everything draining into it. Unlike the right, the left renal vein collects the left suprarenal vein and the left gonadal vein, so nutcracker compression, or a tumour thrombus growing up the vein, presents as a left varicocele that does not empty when the man lies down. A left-sided varicocele in an adult male is a renal cell carcinoma until proven otherwise. This length is also why the left kidney is the one usually harvested for transplant.

structures.name: right ureter
structures.label: Right ureter — the outflow
structures.narration: The renal pelvis funnels down and narrows at the pelviureteric junction to become the ureter, which then runs downwards on the psoas major, crossing the tips of the lumbar transverse processes. The junction is the first of the three constrictions where a stone lodges, and obstruction there backs urine up into the pelvis and calyces — hydronephrosis. Shown here only as the exit from the kidney; the ureter's own course, blood supply and constrictions are a structure in their own right.

structures.name: left ureter
structures.label: Left ureter
structures.narration: Mirror image on the left. Follow it on a plain film and it lies along a line through the tips of the lumbar transverse processes, over the sacroiliac joint, out to the ischial spine and then medially to the bladder — the route that turns a stone into loin-to-groin pain.

structures.name: descending aorta
structures.label: Aorta — the artery's origin
structures.narration: The abdominal aorta lies just left of the midline on the bodies of the lumbar vertebrae and gives its paired renal branches at about L1 to L2. Its position off-centre is the single fact that explains the asymmetry of this whole region: a long right artery and a short right vein, a short left artery and a long left vein.

structures.name: inferior vena cava
structures.label: Inferior vena cava — the vein's destination
structures.narration: Formed at L5 and running up to the right of the aorta, the cava receives both renal veins at about L1. Its closeness on the right is why the right renal vein is short and why a renal cell carcinoma on the right can extend a tumour thrombus into the cava and up towards the right atrium.

structures.name: superior mesenteric artery
structures.label: Superior mesenteric artery — the upper jaw of the nutcracker
structures.narration: Leaves the front of the aorta at L1, just above the renal arteries, and immediately arches forwards. The left renal vein and the third part of the duodenum both have to pass through the angle between it and the aorta — which is why both can be compressed there. It is not the hook that arrests an ascending horseshoe kidney — that is the inferior mesenteric artery, lower down.

structures.name: right adrenal gland
structures.label: Right suprarenal gland
structures.narration: Caps the upper pole but is not part of the kidney. Between the two lies a septum of renal fascia, and that is why a dropped kidney takes its vessels with it but leaves the suprarenal gland where it was.

structures.name: left adrenal gland
structures.label: Left suprarenal gland
structures.narration: Sits on the medial side of the upper pole rather than on top of it. Its vein is long and drains into the left renal vein, unlike the right, which drains into the cava.

structures.name: liver
structures.label: Liver — why the right kidney is lower
structures.narration: The bulk of the right lobe occupies the space above the right kidney and pushes it down. The peritoneal recess between the two — Morison's pouch — is the lowest part of the upper peritoneal cavity when a patient lies supine, and therefore the first window of a trauma scan.

structures.name: spleen
structures.label: Spleen — left anterior relation
structures.narration: Lies against the upper part of the anterior surface of the left kidney, tethered to it by the lienorenal ligament carrying the splenic vessels. Its presence is one of the two clinical points that separate an enlarged spleen from an enlarged left kidney: a kidney is ballotable and you can get above it, a spleen is neither.

structures.name: duodenum
structures.label: Duodenum — over the right hilum
structures.narration: The second part of the duodenum descends directly over the hilum of the right kidney — an anterior relation that must be mobilised, by the Kocher manoeuvre, before the right renal vessels can be reached from in front.

structures.name: pancreatic duct
structures.label: Pancreatic duct — marking the pancreas
structures.narration: The duct runs the length of the gland and so shows where it lies: the body and tail of the pancreas cross the front of the left kidney on their way to the hilum of the spleen. Pancreatic tail surgery is therefore renal surgery's near neighbour.

structures.name: right psoas major
structures.label: Psoas major (right) — the medial bed
structures.narration: Runs down from the lumbar vertebrae and forms the medial part of the muscular bed on which the kidney rests. The ureter descends on its front, and the lumbar plexus is formed within its substance — which is why a psoas abscess tracking down from tuberculous lumbar spine can produce both a groin swelling and referred pain along those nerves.

structures.name: left psoas major
structures.label: Psoas major (left)
structures.narration: The same on the left. Both psoas outlines are visible on a plain abdominal film, and loss of the psoas shadow is a classical sign of retroperitoneal fluid or blood.

structures.name: right quadratus lumborum
structures.label: Quadratus lumborum (right) — the middle of the bed
structures.narration: Runs from the iliac crest up to the twelfth rib and the lumbar transverse processes, forming the middle of the renal bed. Three nerves cross its front behind the kidney, running downwards and laterally: the subcostal, the iliohypogastric and the ilioinguinal. They are the nerves cut or stretched in a loin incision, and the reason a nephrectomy scar can be followed by numbness and a bulging flank.

structures.name: left quadratus lumborum
structures.label: Quadratus lumborum (left)
structures.narration: The left half of the same muscular floor.

structures.name: right transversus abdominis
structures.label: Transversus abdominis — the lateral bed
structures.narration: Its posterior aponeurosis completes the bed laterally. So the kidney lies on four things from medial to lateral: psoas major, quadratus lumborum, the aponeurosis of transversus abdominis, and above them the diaphragm.

structures.name: diaphragm
structures.label: Diaphragm — the roof of the bed
structures.narration: The upper pole of each kidney rests on the diaphragm, so both kidneys descend two or three centimetres with a deep breath — which is what makes a right kidney ballotable on inspiration, and what forces a surgeon to time the puncture in a percutaneous approach. Behind the diaphragm at this level lies the costodiaphragmatic recess of the pleura, and that is the structure a needle passing above the twelfth rib enters.

structures.name: right eleventh rib
structures.label: Eleventh rib
structures.narration: Crosses the back of the LEFT kidney only. The right kidney, sitting lower, is crossed by the twelfth alone. Learn this pair the right way round: it is a favourite one-mark question and it is also the practical difference between entering the chest and not.

structures.name: right twelfth rib
structures.label: Twelfth rib — the surgical landmark
structures.narration: Crosses the back of both kidneys and is the landmark for everything done from behind. The renal angle — between the lower border of the twelfth rib and the lateral border of erector spinae — is where you press for tenderness in pyelonephritis and where the kidney comes closest to the surface. Every posterior approach stays BELOW this rib, because the pleural recess dips behind its medial half and a needle passed above it will find the pleura before it finds the kidney.

structures.name: first lumbar vertebra
structures.label: First lumbar vertebra — the transpyloric plane
structures.narration: The reference level for the whole region. The hilum of the left kidney lies on the transpyloric plane at the lower border of L1; the right hilum is a little below it. The kidneys as a pair span T12 to L3, moving down by half a vertebra on the right.

structures.name: urinary bladder
structures.label: Urinary bladder — where it all ends up
structures.narration: The end of the line. Urine formed in the cortex and medulla passes calyx to pelvis to ureter and reaches the bladder at the vesicoureteric junction — the third and narrowest constriction, and the commonest place for a stone to arrest.

structures.label: Right kidney — upper pole

structures.narration: The upper pole of the right kidney: capped by the suprarenal gland, resting on the diaphragm, and crossed behind by the twelfth rib. It lies about half a vertebral body lower than the left upper pole.

structures.label: Right kidney — lower pole
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: EXTREME -z on FMA7204 (LPS +Z superior, long axis z, span 102.2 mm, 52.7 mm from surface centroid, 1502 vertices)
structures.narration: The lower pole of the right kidney — the part a thin patient's lower pole is balloted at on deep inspiration, the usual destination of an accessory renal artery, and the pole at which the two halves of a horseshoe kidney are fused.

structures.label: Right renal hilum
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: CONTACT — the point on FMA7204 nearest all three structures that pass through the hilum (FMA14752 renal artery 0.31 mm, FMA14335 renal vein 0.44 mm, FMA15571 ureter 0.29 mm · 3 witnesses · spread 21.2 mm over a 102.2 mm organ)
structures.narration: The medial notch where three things pass, front to back: vein, artery, ureter. The second part of the duodenum descends directly over this point, which is why the right renal vessels cannot be reached from in front without a Kocher manoeuvre.

structures.label: Left kidney — upper pole
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: EXTREME +z on FMA7205 (LPS +Z superior, long axis z, span 103.0 mm, 52.7 mm from surface centroid, 1502 vertices)
structures.narration: The upper pole of the left kidney, reaching to about T12 — higher than the right, and crossed behind by both the eleventh and the twelfth ribs. The spleen lies against its front.

structures.label: Left kidney — lower pole
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: EXTREME -z on FMA7205 (LPS +Z superior, long axis z, span 103.0 mm, 52.9 mm from surface centroid, 1502 vertices)
structures.narration: The lower pole of the left kidney, reaching only to about L2 — which is why the left is almost never ballotable and why a mass in the left hypochondrium that you can get above is more likely renal than splenic.

structures.label: Left renal hilum — on the transpyloric plane
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: CONTACT — the point on FMA7205 nearest all three structures that pass through the hilum (FMA14753 renal artery 0.22 mm, FMA14336 renal vein 0.83 mm, FMA15572 ureter 0.21 mm · 3 witnesses · spread 21.6 mm over a 103.0 mm organ)
structures.narration: The left hilum lies almost exactly on the transpyloric plane, at the lower border of L1 — the most useful single level in the abdomen. The same order holds here: vein, artery, ureter from front to back.

structures.label: Pelviureteric junction (right)
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: EXTREME +z on FMA15571 — the ureter model begins at the pelviureteric junction, so the topmost point of that mesh IS the junction (LPS +Z superior, long axis z, span 277.1 mm, 108.3 mm from surface centroid, 1107 vertices)
structures.narration: The first of the three ureteric constrictions, where the funnel of the renal pelvis narrows into the ureter. A stone arrested here obstructs the kidney and dilates the pelvis and calyces into a hydronephrosis. This anchor marks the junction as a point on the ureter, not as a dilated pelvis — the renal pelvis itself has no mesh.

structures.label: Renal angle (costovertebral angle)
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: CONTACT — the renal angle is the corner between the lower border of the twelfth rib and the LATERAL border of erector spinae, and the lateral column of erector spinae is iliocostalis lumborum. The anchor is the point on FMA8533 nearest FMA22740 right iliocostalis lumborum (gap 0.29 mm · 1 witness, so a measurement without a second witness to converge on it)
structures.narration: Where the lower border of the twelfth rib meets the lateral border of erector spinae, the kidney comes closest to the skin. This is where you press or percuss for tenderness in pyelonephritis, and where a percutaneous tract or a biopsy needle enters — always BELOW the rib, because the costodiaphragmatic recess of the pleura dips behind its medial half.

views.title: Where they are, and why they are not level

ops.kind: pushes it half a vertebra lower

views.narration: Both kidneys lie behind the peritoneum on the posterior abdominal wall, one on each side of the vertebral column, tilted so their hila face medially and forwards. They are not level. The left spans about T12 to L2, the right about L1 to L3 — half a vertebral body lower — because the right lobe of the liver takes the space above it. Fix the level by the transpyloric plane at the lower border of L1: the left hilum sits on it. In front, the right kidney is covered by the liver, the second part of the duodenum over its hilum, and the right colic flexure; the left by the stomach, spleen, pancreas, left colic flexure and jejunum. Notice what that means clinically. An enlarged kidney is ballotable, you can get above it, and there is a band of colonic resonance over it; an enlarged spleen moves towards the right iliac fossa, has a notch, is dull to percussion, is not ballotable, and you cannot get above it. Those two signs, taken together, separate the two swellings in the left hypochondrium.

views.title: The bed behind, and the ribs across

ops.kind: roofs the bed and moves them on breathing

views.narration: Turn the body round and the kidney lies on a muscular bed of four structures. From medial to lateral, psoas major, quadratus lumborum and the aponeurosis of transversus abdominis; above all three, the diaphragm. Three nerves run downwards and laterally across quadratus lumborum immediately behind the kidney — subcostal, iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal — and they are what a loin incision must respect. The ribs are the exam point. The twelfth rib crosses the back of BOTH kidneys; the eleventh crosses the LEFT kidney only, because the left is higher. Behind the medial half of the twelfth rib the pleura dips down as the costodiaphragmatic recess, so any posterior approach — a percutaneous nephrolithotomy tract, a renal biopsy, a loin incision — is made below the twelfth rib. Go above it and you enter the pleura before the kidney and produce a pneumothorax. The renal angle itself, between the lower border of the twelfth rib and the lateral border of erector spinae, is where the kidney is nearest the skin: that is where you tap for tenderness in pyelonephritis, and where the needle goes in.

views.title: Coverings, then cortex to pelvis
views.narration: Before you start: what follows is described, not drawn. The kidney here is one solid model, so the coverings, the cortex, the pyramids and the calyces are named against a cut surface that does not show them — only the hilum and the two poles are clickable points on this organ. Cut a kidney in the coronal plane and read it from outside in. Four coverings first, and their order is a standing question: the fibrous renal capsule stripped straight off the surface, then perirenal fat, then renal fascia — the fascia of Gerota — and outside that pararenal fat, heaviest behind. The fascia is open inferiorly, which is why blood or pus from the kidney can track down towards the pelvis, and why a kidney that loses its fat sags: renal ptosis, a mobile kidney with intermittent obstruction. Inside the capsule, the outer third is cortex, granular, and it dips inwards between the pyramids as the renal columns of Bertin. The inner two thirds are medulla, arranged as eight to eighteen striated pyramids whose bases face the cortex and whose apices — the papillae — point into the sinus. Each papilla is pierced by collecting ducts and projects into a minor calyx. Two or three minor calyces join to form a major calyx, two or three major calyces form the renal pelvis, and the pelvis narrows at the pelviureteric junction into the ureter. A nephron straddles the two zones — corpuscle and convoluted tubules in the cortex, the loop of Henle running down into the medulla — which is why the medulla can concentrate urine, and why the outer medulla — where the straight proximal tubule and the thick ascending limb do the most work on the least oxygen — is the zone that dies first in ischaemic acute tubular necrosis.

views.title: In at the hilum, out at the hilum
views.narration: Three things pass through the hilum and their order front to back is fixed: vein, artery, ureter — V, A, U. Say it as you look at the picture and you will not lose the mark. The renal arteries leave the aorta at L1 to L2, just below the superior mesenteric artery. Because the aorta lies left of the midline the right artery is long and passes behind the inferior vena cava, while the left is short. The veins are the mirror: the right is short and joins the cava directly, the left is three times longer, crossing in front of the aorta and behind the superior mesenteric artery. Two consequences follow from that crossing and both are examinable. First, the left renal vein is squeezed in the angle between artery and aorta — the nutcracker — and because it also receives the left gonadal and left suprarenal veins — the gonadal vein is not in this model, so picture it entering from below — that compression, or a tumour thrombus in it, shows up as a left varicocele that does not empty on lying down. Second, the left kidney is the one taken for transplantation, because a long vein is easier to sew. Inside the kidney the artery divides into five segmental branches which are true end arteries with no anastomoses between them, so each segment can be resected — and each can be infarcted — on its own.

views.title: From glomerulus to bladder
views.narration: Everything microscopic in this beat — glomeruli, tubules, loops, collecting ducts — is described, not drawn; what moves on screen is the trace from kidney to ureter to bladder. Urine formation in one line of anatomy. About a fifth of the cardiac output — over a litre a minute — enters by the renal arteries and reaches roughly a million glomeruli in the cortex of each kidney. Filtration there produces about 180 litres a day of filtrate; the tubules reabsorb ninety-nine per cent of it, so one to two litres leaves as urine. The convoluted tubules sit in the cortex, the loops of Henle and the collecting ducts run down through the pyramids, and the ducts open on the papilla into a minor calyx. From there the route is fixed and worth reciting: minor calyx, major calyx, renal pelvis, pelviureteric junction, ureter, vesicoureteric junction, bladder. Smooth muscle in the pelvis and ureter drives peristaltic waves — urine does not simply run downhill — and it is that peristalsis working against an obstruction which produces the severe colicky pain of a stone.

views.title: Reading the clinic off the anatomy
views.narration: Five presentations, all readable off what you have just seen. Renal colic: a stone lodges at the pelviureteric junction, at the pelvic brim, or at the vesicoureteric junction, and the pain follows the segmental nerve supply of the organ it is sitting in. The kidney itself refers to T10 to L1; the ureter refers to T11 to L2. That one segment of difference is the loin-to-groin march: a stone at the pelviureteric junction hurts in the loin at the kidney's own levels, and as it descends the pain drops with it into the groin, the scrotum or the labium on the ureter's lower levels. The pain is colicky and the patient rolls about rather than lying still. Pyelonephritis: constant loin pain with fever, and tenderness elicited in the renal angle below the twelfth rib. Obstruction: back-pressure dilates the pelvis and calyces into a hydronephrosis, which is why an obstructed kidney is a surgical emergency and an unobstructed one is not. Trauma and access: the kidney is retroperitoneal, so bleeding is often contained by renal fascia, and every posterior approach stays below the twelfth rib to keep out of the pleura. And tumour: a renal cell carcinoma presents late with the triad of loin pain, a mass and haematuria, spreads along the renal vein into the cava, and on the left announces itself as a varicocele that will not empty. Two developmental variants complete the picture — the horseshoe kidney fused at its lower poles and caught under the inferior mesenteric artery during its ascent, and the pelvic kidney that never ascended at all, which is felt as a pelvic mass and injured in pelvic surgery.

gaps: The kidney is one solid model. The catalog holds no renal cortex, medulla, pyramid, papilla, column of Bertin, minor calyx, major calyx or renal pelvis, so beat three teaches the internal architecture entirely by narration over a CROSS_SECTION cut of the whole organ. A student can see that the organ has an inside but cannot click a pyramid or a calyx. Every internal name is carried in match.terms and in the kidney structures' own terms[], so a note that says 'column of Bertin' still opens this scene at the right subject. An internal-structure model, or a companion diagram-mode scene of the coronal section, is the single highest-value addition for this topic.

There is no renal capsule, no perirenal fat, no renal fascia and no pararenal fat. The four coverings are one of the two things most reliably asked about the kidney and none of them has a mesh. They are narrated in beat three and PEEL_LAYER is authored there so that the beat becomes real the day layered models exist; today the op degrades to hiding the organ layer, which is an honest approximation of stripping the coverings but not a demonstration of them.

The renal pelvis has no separate model, so the pelviureteric junction is shown as the point where the ureter model begins rather than as a named narrowing. Hydronephrosis therefore cannot be shown as a dilated pelvis, only described.

CORRECTED 2026-08-29: the previous note here said no anchors could be authored because the meshes were not in the local decimated set. That was stale — FMA7204, FMA7205 and FMA15571 are all in meshes-lite/, and eight anchors have now been measured: both upper and lower poles by EXTREME ±z, both hila by CONTACT against the renal artery, renal vein and ureter (three converging witnesses each, largest gap 0.83 mm), and the pelviureteric junction as the topmost point of the ureter mesh. An eighth anchor, the renal angle, was very nearly not authored on the same false reasoning: the first draft of this note said the catalog holds no erector spinae. It holds no mesh under that name, nor under sacrospinalis, but it holds all three of the muscle's columns under their own names — iliocostalis lumborum, longissimus thoracis, spinalis thoracis — and the renal angle is defined against the LATERAL column, so a contact between the twelfth rib and iliocostalis lumborum measures it directly (0.29 mm, one witness). Searching once for the clinical name would have lost it. What still cannot be anchored is the pelvic-brim and vesicoureteric constrictions, which sit on the ureter's course rather than at a measurable extreme of it. The eight authored anchors carry status needs-review: the measurement and its evidence are in each calibrated_by, but nobody has yet opened them in the viewer.

The peritoneum is absent, as it is throughout this corpus, so 'retroperitoneal' is asserted rather than shown. Morison's pouch is described against the liver and the right kidney, both of which exist.

The five segmental arteries are not in the catalog; only the main renal artery trunk on each side is. The end-artery principle and the avascular plane of Brodel are therefore narrated against a single vessel.

The gonadal veins are not in the catalog, so the left varicocele story is told through the left renal vein alone. This weakens beat four's strongest clinical hook, since the vein whose obstruction the student must picture cannot be drawn.

This scene does not claim to cover 'Ureters', 'Suprarenal (adrenal) gland' or 'Abdominal aorta & IVC' even though all of them appear in it. The ureters are here as the kidney's outflow, not as a course with three constrictions and a segmental blood supply; the suprarenal glands are here as a relation; the aorta and cava are here only to fix where the renal vessels begin and end. All three remain on the worklist as separate curriculum entries.

Ribs are single-sided models in the catalog. The eleventh rib shown is the right eleventh rib, used to teach a left-sided relation, because it is the same bone mirrored and the teaching point is the level rather than the side. The label and narration say plainly that it is the left kidney that the eleventh rib crosses, so nothing is misrepresented, but a student rotating the scene will see the rib on the wrong side.

Beat two names the three nerves crossing quadratus lumborum behind the kidney — subcostal, iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal — and the costodiaphragmatic recess of the pleura. None is in the catalog (searched under each name, and under pleura: nothing in 934 entries). They are the reason every posterior approach stays below the twelfth rib, so they are taught in words and not drawn.
